_notes: Line landmarks with known poses on procedural scenes (parallel_lines*), plus the paper's joint pose/point/line factor-graph optimisation on Open-Structure ICL-NUIM and TartanAir sequences (open_structure_joint_ba; keyframe subsets, Sim(3)-aligned ATE). The hidden test generates or loads its instances inside eval/test/ and runs every solver in scripts/methods/ on them. All coefficients are magnitudes; direction comes from higher_is_better.

parallel_lines.description: Recover 3D line landmarks (2-3 declared parallel groups plus individual lines) from noisy multi-view segment observations with known poses; 8 cameras around the scene, 1.0 px noise, partial visibility and truncated segments.
parallel_lines.notes: Result values are the paper's Table 6 parameter counts expressed per line: StructRiemanLine uses the minimal count of the true structure (44 for 20 lines, error 0), independent 4n representations use 80, i.e. (80 - 44) / 20 = 1.8 excess parameters per line. The paper reports no number on this synthetic scale for the angular and novel-view metrics; its Table 4 values are kept under _paper_reported for context only.

median_direction_error_deg.description: Median, over every line of every scene, of the unsigned angle (deg) between the estimated and the true 3D line direction (paper Table 4, 'Dir.').

p90_direction_error_deg.description: 90th percentile of the same per-line direction errors (paper Fig. 5: tail of the error distribution).

median_normal_error_deg.description: Median unsigned angle (deg) between the estimated and true Plucker normal (moment) vectors, world frame at the first camera (paper Table 4, 'Norm.').

p90_normal_error_deg.description: 90th percentile of the per-line normal errors.

novel_view_line_rmse_px.description: RMS distance (px, each distance clipped at 100) from noise-free projections of the true segment endpoints into held-out cameras, never given to the method, to the projected estimated line.

param_count_error_per_line.description: |effective - minimal| line parameters per line. Effective = 2 x (distinct estimated directions) + 2 x (lines), counted from the output geometry; minimal = the same count for the true scene structure (paper Table 6: 2n + 2 for n parallel lines vs 4n).

table4._source: Paper Table 4 (TartanAir, median line errors in degrees, Dir./Norm.). Real SLAM sequences with joint pose optimisation; not on this gym's scale.

table6._source: Paper Table 6 / Sec. 5 (box sequence): 20 line landmarks need 80 parameters with the 4n orthonormal form and 44 with StructRiemanLine (2n + 2 per parallel group).

parallel_lines_mislabeled.description: Where the paper's method falls short: the declared parallel associations contain errors (1-2 members per group are 3-10 degrees off parallel, and half of the scenes contain one grossly wrong member), as produced by imperfect vanishing-point clustering. 8 cameras, 1.2 px noise.
parallel_lines_mislabeled.notes: Result values are the paper's Table 6 parameter counts expressed per line: StructRiemanLine uses the minimal count of the true structure (44 for 20 lines, error 0), independent 4n representations use 80, i.e. (80 - 44) / 20 = 1.8 excess parameters per line. The paper reports no number on this synthetic scale for the angular and novel-view metrics; its Table 4 values are kept under _paper_reported for context only. This setting is not in the paper; the paper assumes correct associations, so its Table 6 numbers describe the correctly grouped case only.

open_structure_joint_ba.description: Joint optimisation of camera poses, point landmarks and line landmarks from the initial co-visibility factor graph of an Open-Structure sequence (paper Sec. 4-5, Tables 2-4). Hidden test: 6 held-out sequences (ICL-NUIM livingroom2, livingroom3, office2, office3; TartanAir hospital, carwelding), 4 keyframe-phase instances each (at most 150 keyframes), scored against the datasets' own ground-truth trajectories and line landmarks.
open_structure_joint_ba.notes: Scaled reproduction of Tables 2-4: keyframe subsets instead of every frame; ATE RMSE uses Sim(3) alignment (the factor graph has 2D measurements only, so its scale is a free gauge) and is the geometric mean over instances; 1 px Gaussian noise is added to the TartanAir measurements, which Open-Structure provides as exact projections. The ate_rmse_cm values below are the geometric means of the paper's own per-sequence ATE RMSE (SE(3)-aligned, every frame; Tables 2-3) over the six held-out sequences, given for orientation only: they are not on exactly this gym's scale. param_count_error_per_line follows the paper's Table 6 (2n + 2 per parallel group vs 4n), as in the procedural experiments.

ate_rmse_cm.description: Absolute trajectory error (cm): RMSE of keyframe camera centres after Sim(3) alignment to the ground-truth trajectory, geometric mean over instances (paper Tables 2-3).

rotation_rmse_deg.description: RMS rotation error (deg) of the keyframe orientations after the same alignment, geometric mean over instances (paper Sec. 5: rotational consistency).

median_direction_error_deg.description: Median unsigned angle (deg) between estimated and ground-truth line directions, after the trajectory alignment, pooled over every scored line (paper Table 4, 'Dir.').

p90_direction_error_deg.description: 90th percentile of the same direction errors (paper Fig. 5: error tails).

median_normal_error_deg.description: Median unsigned angle (deg) between estimated and ground-truth Plucker normal (moment) vectors in the ground-truth frame (paper Table 4, 'Norm.').

param_count_error_per_line.description: |effective - minimal| line parameters per scored line: effective = 2 x (distinct estimated directions) + 2 x (lines); minimal = the same count for the ground-truth direction classes (paper Table 6).

table2_ate_rmse_cm._source: Paper Table 2 (ICL-NUIM, translation APE RMSE in cm, SE(3)-aligned, every frame).

table3_ate_rmse_cm._source: Paper Table 3 (TartanAir, translation APE RMSE in cm). Its 'Rot.' column matches the SE(3)-aligned median translation error of the initial graphs, so it is not used here.

table4_median_line_errors_deg._source: Paper Table 4 (TartanAir, median line direction / normal errors in degrees).

open_structure_joint_ba_clustered.description: Same task and hidden sequences as open_structure_joint_ba, but the declared parallel groups come from a vanishing-direction clustering of the initial map's line directions (10 deg), as a SLAM front end would produce them, instead of the dataset's exact associations: groups contain some non-parallel lines (truly 1-13 deg off) and miss some members. Different keyframe phases, world frames, ids and noise draws from open_structure_joint_ba.
open_structure_joint_ba_clustered.notes: Where the paper's method falls short on the paper's own data: it trusts the declared groups (only a coarse 25 deg consistency check). The paper reports no numbers for this setting; the ate_rmse_cm values below are the same geometric means of the paper's Tables 2-3 (dataset associations) over the six held-out sequences, for orientation only. Same metrics, coefficients and scaling notes as open_structure_joint_ba.
